label: Open
title: Open the project
question: Can I use this downloaded project?
lead: Open the file and let Studio read it on your computer. The first screen tells you what kind of file it is and whether Studio can prepare a U1 copy from it. No prepared copy is written yet.

evidence.note: The example project is `demo_offplate_foreign.3mf` from the [examples folder](@examples); the STL is `sample_cube.stl`.

means.meaning: Studio can write a U1 copy from this file.
means.action: Go on to the checks. This is advice about preparing, not a promise about the print.

means.meaning: The checks found something worth fixing before you slice, such as an object off the plate.
means.action: Read the checks (next stage); many problems have a fix in the stage after.

means.seen: “This STL does not include creator slicer settings.”
means.meaning: An STL is a shape only: no colors and no print settings. Studio uses a U1 starter profile unless you pick another Orca profile.
means.action: Nothing is wrong. You choose the settings in Orca.

means.seen: **Studio could not open this file as a 3MF project.** (in Compatibility)
means.meaning: Studio could not read the file as a 3MF. It may be damaged, inaccessible or not a 3MF.
means.action: Download it again. The Workspace can look normal for a damaged file, so trust what Compatibility says.

steps: Press **Open a model** (top of the sidebar, or the large button on Home), or drag an `.stl` or `.3mf` onto the Studio window.
Studio opens the **Workspace** and reads the file locally.
Read the status line, the verdict banner and **What's in this design**.
success: You see the file name and **Checked — here's what we found. Press Prepare U1 copy when you're set.**
A verdict banner appears, for example **Can prepare a U1 copy**.
Your original file is untouched, and no prepared copy has been written.

differs.if: Nothing happens after choosing a file.
differs.then: The file may be damaged, or it may not be an STL or 3MF file. Download it again. For a 3MF, open **Compatibility**, which should say “Studio could not open this file as a 3MF project.”

differs.if: I do not have a project to try.
differs.then: Use the example files in the [examples folder](@examples). Open `demo_offplate_foreign.3mf` to follow along.

notes.text: Opening a file never changes it. Studio is local-first: the file is read on your computer and nothing is uploaded.

next.why: Next question: what needs attention before I slice?

label: Check
title: Read the checks
question: What needs attention before slicing?
lead: Studio compares the project with the U1 and with Snapmaker Orca's expectations. You do not need to read every line. What matters is telling a confirmed problem from a heads-up, and both from something Studio cannot know.

evidence.note: Open **This print**, or **Compatibility** (Advanced sidebar; **More tools** in Simple view).

means.seen: **1 object is outside the U1's printable area.**
means.meaning: An object hangs off the plate. Studio names the object, the edge and the distance.
means.action: Decide whether it is misplaced or too big (next stage).

means.meaning: Likely to cause trouble in Orca. For a downloaded 3MF it usually means settings from another printer; the text says the model itself may be fine.
means.action: Read the **Do this:** line. Preparing a U1 copy is designed to handle this.

means.meaning: Studio starts at 100 and takes points off for each risk signal it found. The percentage is not a probability of print success. **Few risks** means the score is at least 75, so a signal may still have cost points. The line under it shows the percentage; the bullet list of signals appears only below 75.
means.action: Review any listed signals before printing.

means.meaning: Worth knowing, often something Studio cannot verify, such as spacing between objects.
means.action: Check it in Orca (**Arrange**, collision warnings).

means.meaning: Studio lacks information it needs for this check. It is not a problem found; it is a gap.
means.action: Connect the printer, or check it yourself. See the unknown-versus-confirmed example in stage 6.

means.meaning: Studio checked and found nothing wrong.
means.action: Read any action listed on the card. It is advice, not a guarantee.

steps: Open **This print** for the whole job, or **Compatibility** for the full list (the **Open the full checks** link takes you there).
Read **Object placement** first. Studio can move this example onto the plate, and preparing a U1 copy also adjusts incompatible project settings.
Skim the cards. For each, read the label, then its **Do this:** line. Open **Technical detail** only if you are curious.
Make a short list: confirmed problems, things to check in Orca, things Studio cannot tell.
success: You can say which findings are facts and which are gaps.
You know whether the next step is a fix in Studio (stage 3) or a job for Orca.

differs.if: The findings say “Invalid value for …”. Is my model broken?
differs.then: Usually not. The text says the model may be fine and the project settings are for another printer.
Studio first tries to reach a printer. When none answers, the cards switch to **Printer not found** and **Studio can’t tell**.

differs.if: My findings differ from the example.
differs.then: They describe your own file. The labels mean the same thing.

notes.text: “Studio can’t tell” means Studio has no way to read the fact from your printer. It does not mean your printer cannot do it. Studio can also say it when the file leaves a fact out.
The checks are read-only. Studio never edits your file while diagnosing it.

next.why: Next question: what can Studio fix, and how should I prepare my copy?

label: Prepare
title: Fix and prepare
question: What can Studio fix, and how should I prepare my copy?
lead: Studio can write a repositioned copy and a U1 copy. It fixes only what one safe action can fix, and it tells you when it will not. Both actions write new files; your original stays as it is.

shots.label: The Workspace: preparation mode and placement

evidence.note: The example project has one 20 mm object that hangs 55 mm past the right edge.

means.seen: **Move onto the plate (saves a copy)** is offered
means.meaning: One shift of the whole layout brings every object onto the plate. Studio can do it and verify the result.
means.action: Press it, then prepare the moved copy.

means.seen: No Move button: “Moving the objects as one piece would not bring them all on, so Studio will not guess.”
means.meaning: A single shift cannot fix it: the layout is wider than the plate in its current orientation.
means.action: Open the project in Orca and use **Arrange**; if an object still does not fit, rotate, resize or split it.

means.meaning: Keeps the creator's print settings and changes only the minimum for Orca to open the file.
means.action: The right choice for a downloaded model.

means.meaning: Replaces the creator's settings with Studio's U1 defaults: speed, temperature, retraction, supports and cooling change.
means.action: Use this when the file came from a very different printer.

means.meaning: Studio prepared the file for the U1, but the checks still list things for you.
means.action: Handle them in Orca (stage 5).

steps: If **Object placement** offers **Move onto the plate (saves a copy)**, press it. Studio writes `…_placed_U1.3mf` next to your original.
Press **Open a model** and choose that moved copy. (The move and the U1 preparation are separate actions.)
Leave **Preserve creator settings** selected unless you have a reason, then press **Prepare U1 copy**.

Optional, if you track spools: on **Compatibility**, pick a spool and an installed preset for each color under **Project materials**, press **Review & prepare**, read the review, then **Prepare with these choices**.
success: You see **U1 copy created — review setup before slicing**, followed by a note that your original file is not modified.
New files beside your original, for example `…_placed_U1_SnapmakerU1.3mf`. You may also see a `.orig.3mf` snapshot Studio keeps next to a prepared copy.
When you open the prepared copy, **Object placement** says the object sits inside the printable area.

differs.then: Read the placement message. Either every object already fits, no single shift brings them all on, or Studio will not move this project (it never repositions multi-plate projects). Work through the placement example above.

differs.if: The prepared copy still shows warnings.
differs.then: Studio prepares the file for the U1; it does not fix every setting. Read **Your fix plan**: each step is marked **Do this in Studio** or **Do this in Orca**.
Two slots share one preset but the project declares different vendors or types for them. Choose a different preset for one slot; Studio does not edit the project for you.

notes.text: **Move onto the plate** only changes where objects sit. To get a U1 copy that is also on the plate, prepare the moved copy. Preparing the original on its own does not move anything.
Your original is never modified. Every action here writes a new file.

next.why: Next question: what changed in the prepared copy?

label: Review
title: Review what changed
question: What changed in the prepared copy?
lead: Studio does not ask you to trust the copy. It lists what it kept, what it changed, what it could not carry over and what it could not check, and you can always return to your original.

shots.label: The fidelity report and the change ledger

evidence.note: These cards appear on the Workspace right after preparing, and on **This print** under **2. Prepared**.

means.seen: **What survived preparing this copy** — 14 kept · 2 changed
means.meaning: A comparison of what Studio can identify in both files. Kept means the value reached the copy, not that Orca uses it: read any note on the row.
means.action: Expand **What Studio changed** and look at each line.

means.meaning: Settings changed only so the project suits the U1, for example the printer identity. Where a setting was outside its valid range, Studio used the U1 default.
means.action: Skim **Before and after**; flag anything that surprises you.

means.meaning: Suggestions Studio did not apply.
means.action: Nothing changes unless you choose **Prepare another copy with recommended settings**.

means.meaning: Something in the original was left behind, or Studio could not establish what happened to it. Read each row's reason.
means.action: Check that setting in Orca.

means.meaning: Studio could not verify this item: it may be an unexplained change, or something it could not compare.
means.action: Compare that setting with your original in Orca before slicing, and report it.

steps: After preparing, scroll to **What survived preparing this copy** and note the counts.
Expand **What Studio changed (n)**, then **What stayed the same (n)**.
Open **Changes Studio made** and **Before and after** for the old and new values; long values are shortened on screen.
Read **Your fix plan**: anything marked **Do this in Orca** is for the next stage.
success: You can name what Studio changed and what it left to you.
You know where **Return to the original** is, and that the original was never changed.

differs.if: My numbers differ from the example.
differs.then: They describe your file. The report has the same sections.

differs.if: I want to undo a preparation.
differs.then: There is nothing to undo: your original was never changed. Delete the copy if you do not want it.

notes.text: **Return to the original** never writes to your original. Everything Studio makes is a new file.

next.why: Next question: what must I review in Orca?

label: Slice in Orca
title: Slice in Snapmaker Orca
question: What must I review in Orca before slicing?
lead: Studio hands the prepared copy to Snapmaker Orca and stops. Orca slices. Your job is the review Studio cannot do for you.

shots.label: The prepared result in the installed Studio

evidence.note: Orca's own window is not shown here: see “What this guide does not show” on the home page.

means.meaning: A one-way handoff. Studio opens the file in Orca and does nothing else with it.
means.action: Press it, or use **Copy path** and open the file in Orca yourself.

means.meaning: Studio could not find Orca on this computer.
means.action: Install it from its [releases page](@orca), then use **Copy path** and open the prepared file from inside Orca.

means.meaning: A step Studio cannot do: for example turning on supports, or using Arrange and checking spacing.
means.action: Do it before slicing.

means.meaning: A preset you made yourself is named in the copy, but Studio cannot confirm Orca applies its temperature, flow and cooling.
means.action: Check the filament in Orca before slicing.

means.meaning: Orca treats the project's settings as a customization, which can happen when the creator's tuned settings are kept.
means.action: Review the settings in Orca before slicing.

steps: On the prepared result, press **Open in Snapmaker Orca** (or **Copy path**).
In Orca, check: the printer is **Snapmaker U1**; the filaments and colors match what you will load; the objects are on the plate (use **Arrange** if unsure); supports are set the way you want.
Slice in Orca (**Slice plate**).
Export the G-code (the file of printer instructions) with Orca's own export command and note where it is saved. Menu wording can differ between Orca versions.
Keep the exported `.gcode`. Save the Orca project too if you want your Orca settings kept.
success: Orca opens your prepared copy, and Studio stays as it was: it does not control Orca and does not slice.
You have an exported `.gcode` file for the next stage.

differs.then: Install Orca from its [releases page](@orca), then use **Copy path** and open the prepared file from inside Orca.

differs.if: Studio says “Couldn’t launch Snapmaker Orca — open the file from Orca instead.”
differs.then: Open the prepared file from inside Orca; **Copy path** helps you find it.

differs.if: Studio says “Couldn’t find the prepared file — try preparing it again.”
differs.then: The copy was moved or deleted. Prepare it again.

notes.text: The prepared copy is a starting point. Always review it in Orca before slicing: Studio's report from the previous stage lists what it changed.
This guide has no screenshots of Snapmaker Orca's own window, so Orca's menus are described in general terms only.

next.why: Next question: does the sliced job match my printer and loaded materials?

label: Check the job
title: Check the sliced job
question: Does the sliced job match my printer and loaded materials?
lead: Everything before this checked your project. This stage checks the G-code Orca produced, which is the file the printer actually runs. Studio reads it, compares it with the project and, when a printer is connected, with the printer.

shots.label: An example job whose header names a U1, no printer connected
An example job whose header names a different printer

evidence.note: The pictures use small example jobs written for this guide, not real prints.

means.seen: **Sliced for a different printer** (WORTH SETTLING FIRST)
means.meaning: The job names a printer other than the U1, or a name Studio does not recognize as the U1.
means.action: Re-slice the model in Orca with a U1 profile.

means.seen: **Studio cannot tie this job to your project**
means.meaning: Nothing in either file identifies the model, so Studio cannot tell whether this job was sliced from the project you checked.
means.action: Make sure you picked the right file.

means.seen: **Tools this job needs** / **The bed this was sliced for** / **Nozzle size** — STUDIO CAN'T CHECK THIS
means.meaning: Studio needs information from your printer to check these.
means.action: Connect the printer in Printer Hub, or check them yourself.

means.seen: **Sliced for the machine Studio prepares for** — LOOKS RIGHT
means.meaning: The job's header says it was sliced for a U1. Studio reads the header; it has not simulated the commands.
means.action: Read any action on the card. Advice, not a guarantee.

means.seen: **What the printer will actually do**: sliced by, for, layers, estimated time, filament
means.meaning: Metadata and estimates read from the G-code, not a simulation or a measured result.
means.action: Compare them with what you expect.

steps: Open **After Slicing** (Advanced sidebar, **More tools**, or stage 3 of **This print**).
Optional: type the folder where Orca saves exports and press **Watch this folder**. Studio looks only while **After Slicing** or **This print** is open.
Otherwise drag the `.gcode` onto the window or paste its full path under **Open the G-code your slicer produced**, then press **Check this job**.
Read **Ready to send?** and then each finding. Sort them into confirmed, worth checking and unknown.
Read **What the printer will actually do** and **What to load** (what each slot needs).
success: You know which findings are facts, and which are gaps that still need checking.
You can say what you will do about each: re-slice, check yourself, or connect the printer.

differs.if: Nothing appears in the watched folder.
differs.then: Check that it is the folder Orca exports to, and that **After Slicing** or **This print** is open. You can always paste the file's path.

differs.if: Studio says “that file does not exist”.
differs.then: Studio could not find a file at that path. Copy the full path of the exported `.gcode` again.

differs.if: Many items say “Studio can’t check this”.
differs.then: That is expected when no printer is connected. Connect the printer (see the task) or check those items yourself.

notes.text: On its own, Studio reads only the file. With no printer connected it cannot tell which tools are present, whether slots are loaded, whether the bed matches or which nozzle is fitted (unless you confirmed the nozzle yourself).
Studio reads and never changes your G-code, and it never sends anything on its own. Printing starts only when you start it on the printer or confirm it in Printer Hub.
This guide shows Printer Hub before a printer is connected; it has no screenshot of a connected printer.

next.why: After this you are at the printer: load the filament, then start the print yourself.
